newsitem.title: USA: Marco storm still off Cuban coast, but weakens.
newsitem.headline: Marco storm still off Cuban coast, but weakens.

text.p: The remnants of Hurricane Marco weakened to a tropical depression on Tuesday, clearing the way for the Cuban government to lift all tropical storm warnings, the U.S. National Hurricane Centre said.

At 10 a.m. EST (1300 GMT), the late-season storm was centred 140 miles (225 km) south-southeast of Cabo San Antonio on the western tip of Cuba. Its exact position was latitude 19.9 north and longitude 84.3 west.
The storm was stationary with maximum sustained winds of 35 mph (56 kph), and was expected to weaken further, hurricane centre forecasters said.
On Monday, the storm unexpectedly reached tropical storm strength again after waxing and waning in the Caribbean Sea for the past week. Two deaths in Nicaragua were blamed on Marco's torrential rain.
The weakening of the storm was good news for Cuba, which was pounded by Hurricane Lili on Oct. 17 and 18, destroying about 5,000 homes and damaging crops, power lines and communications.
